name: La Loge
funding: Flemish Government, French Community, VGC, Ixelles, COCOF, Brussels-Capital Region and the National Lottery, plus First Sight members.
watch: Intimate non-profit space situated in a former Masonic temple in Ixelles. Dedicated to contemporary art, architectural theory, and slow, discursive commissions.
records_note: Names its public funders and its board, undated, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: The Showroom
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation (NPO), Paul Hamlyn Foundation, Esmée Fairbairn Foundation. Registered Charity No. 1055262.
watch: Known for its landmark 'Communal Knowledge' program, linking international artists with local housing estates and immigrant communities.

name: Raven Row
funding: Funded by Alex Sainsbury, who says the money is his, through the Glass-House Trust he settled.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the About page names its one funder, and four board members are named.

name: Auto Italia South East
funding: Arts Council England, British Council, and non-commercial trusts. Registered Charity No. 1172824.
watch: Artist-run organisation and research platform dedicated to the support of queer, trans, working-class and migrant voices. Originating in a Peckham car showroom, it remains fiercely autonomous.

name: Cubitt
funding: Arts Council England NPO, Islington Council, Outset Contemporary Art Fund, artist studio rents. Registered Charity No. 1049602.

name: Transmission Gallery
funding: Creative Scotland, member subscriptions, grassroots fundraisers.
watch: Historic artist-run cooperative space founded in 1983 by graduates of Glasgow School of Art to provide an alternative to commercial galleries and municipal conservatism. Governed by a rotating unpaid artist committee.

name: Project Arts Centre
funding: The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon, Dublin City Council, non-commercial ticket sales. Registered Charity No. 20008447.
watch: Ireland's premier multidisciplinary contemporary arts institute in Temple Bar.

name: Badischer Kunstverein
funding: City of Karlsruhe Department of Cultural Affairs, State of Baden-Württemberg, membership dues. Registered Non-Profit Association (e.V.).

name: Kunstverein München
funding: Members' association; only project funders visible (Flanders State of the Art, Danish Arts Foundation).
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the board page names nine members and the sponsors page shows eleven logos with no names or dates.

name: Secession (Wiener Secession)
funding: City of Vienna and the federal ministry. Erste Bank is main sponsor; annual partners Neuroth, Dorotheum and LG; 2026 partners Arbeiterkammer and UNIQA.
watch: The world's oldest independent artist-run exhibition house, founded in 1897 by Gustav Klimt and fellow secessionists under the motto: 'To every age its art, to art its freedom'.
records_note: Shows partners mostly as logos under 2026 headings and states a third of its budget is public; no reports, accounts or board named.

name: Centre d'Art Contemporain Genève
funding: City of Geneva (Ville de Genève), Republic and Canton of Geneva, Swiss Federal Office of Culture (OFC), Loterie Romande. Audited public accounts.

name: Tensta konsthall
funding: Swedish Arts Council (Kulturrådet), City of Stockholm, Region Stockholm. Complete non-profit accounting.
watch: Located in the modernist Tensta suburb of Stockholm, it directly addresses migration, working-class housing struggles, and civic solidarity.
